My Health Records Act 2012 and My Health Records Rules 2026

Act C2026C00277; Rules F2026L00392 · in force; Act compilation No. 18 from 2026-07-01; Rules 2026 from 2026-03-31 (replaced the 2016 Rule) · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Registered healthcare provider organisations, repository operators and portal operators.

We fix
sloptopop finds evidence of a breach of this point in your code, and at least one of those checks has an automatic fix that has passed review on real code.
We detect
sloptopop finds evidence of a breach of this point in your code, and you fix it.
Coming soon
sloptopop does not check this point yet.

A check shows a breach in code; it does not certify that a point is met. List scraped from the publisher's document on 2026-11-01, the publisher's document on 2026-11-01. A point here means: Act compilation No. 18 (C2026C00277) and Rules 2026 as made (F2026L00392): section, subsection, paragraph, sub-paragraph, numbered table row; Schedule clause. Chapter/Part/Division headings group only; notes are informative; definition limbs stay inside the definition text of their provision. The Rules' Schedule 1 only repeals earlier instruments, so its repeal items are spent amending matter and stay out..

Act s 45A Condition of registration—handling old records that are works subject to copyrightOrganisations must not upload older copyright works where use would infringe copyright, as a registration condition.
Act s 45A(1) Old works must not be uploaded if it would be an infringement of copyright to use the work for healthcare or related purposesRule covers works created before the Copyright Act provision commences. Coming soon
Act s 45A(2) Old works must not be uploaded if it would be an infringement of copyright to use the work for healthcare or related purposesDo not upload an old work if the permitted uses would infringe its copyright.
Act s 45A(2)(a) Covers acts for purposes where the Act requires or authorises health information handling. Coming soon
Act s 45A(2)(b) Covers acts in a serious-threat situation permitted under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 45A(2)(c) Covers acts in a permitted health situation under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 45A(2)(d) Covers other healthcare or health information purposes prescribed by regulations. Coming soon
Act s 45A(3) Old works must not be uploaded if it would be an infringement of copyright to use the work for healthcare or related purposesComplying with the old-works copyright duty is a condition of registration. Coming soon
Act s 45B Condition of registration—handling old sound recordings and cinematograph films that are subject to copyrightOrganisations must not upload older sound recordings or films if use would infringe copyright.
Act s 45B(1) Rule covers recordings and films made before the Copyright Act provision commences. Coming soon
Act s 45B(2) Do not upload an old recording or film if permitted uses would infringe its copyright.
Act s 45B(2)(a) Covers acts for purposes where the Act requires or authorises health information handling. Coming soon
Act s 45B(2)(b) Covers acts in a serious-threat situation permitted under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 45B(2)(c) Covers acts in a permitted health situation under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 45B(2)(d) Covers other healthcare or health information purposes prescribed by regulations. Coming soon
Act s 45B(3) Complying with the old recordings and films duty is a registration condition. Coming soon
Act s 45C Liability where work uploaded in breach of section 45A or 45BAnyone harmed by an upload breaching copyright rules can sue for losses within six years.
Act s 45C(1) A person suffering loss from a breach of the copyright upload rules may bring a court action.
Act s 45C(1)(a) Action may be brought in the Federal Court. Coming soon
Act s 45C(1)(b) Action may be brought in the Federal Circuit and Family Court, Division 2. Coming soon
Act s 45C(1)(c) Action may be brought in a State or Territory court with jurisdiction. Coming soon
Act s 45C(2) Time limit: six years from when the loss or damage occurred. Coming soon
Act s 45C(3) Damages may include the claimant's legal costs from copyright infringement proceedings. Coming soon
Act s 46 Condition of registration—non ‐ discrimination in providing healthcare to a healthcare recipient who does not have a My Health Record etc.Providers must not refuse or disfavour patients over lacking a record or their access settings.
Act s 46(1) Healthcare recipient who is not registeredRegistration condition: no refusal or discrimination against patients without a My Health Record.
Act s 46(1)(a) Do not refuse care because the patient has not registered. Coming soon
Act s 46(1)(b) Do not otherwise treat patients unfavourably for being unregistered. Coming soon
Act s 46(2) Registered healthcare recipient’s access controlsRegistration condition: no refusal or discrimination because of a patient's chosen access controls.
Act s 46(2)(a) Do not refuse care because the patient set particular record access controls. Coming soon
Act s 46(2)(b) Do not otherwise discriminate against patients for their access control choices. Coming soon
Act s 47 Persons may apply for registration as a repository operator, a portal operator or a contracted service providerPeople may apply to register as repository operator, portal operator or contracted service provider.
Act s 47(1) A person may apply for one of three registration kinds.
Act s 47(1)(a) Registration as a repository operator may be sought. Coming soon
Act s 47(1)(b) Registration as a portal operator may be sought. Coming soon
Act s 47(1)(c) Registration as a contracted service provider may be sought. Coming soon
Act s 47(2) Repository operator applications must name each repository the registration would cover. Coming soon
Act s 48 When a person is eligible for registration as a repository operator, a portal operator or a contracted service providerEligibility for operator or provider registration: Rules compliance, accepting conditions, Australian control, and state privacy coverage.
Act s 48(a) Applicant must comply with Rules applying to that registration kind. Coming soon
Act s 48(b) Applicant must have agreed to the conditions the System Operator imposes. Coming soon
Act s 48(c) Repository and portal operators must keep central management and control in Australia throughout registration. Coming soon
Act s 48(d) State or Territory operators lacking a designated privacy law must be prescribed under the Privacy Act.
Act s 48(d)(i) Applies to operators that are State or Territory authorities or instrumentalities. Coming soon
Act s 48(d)(ii) Applies where the State or Territory body is not bound by a designated privacy law. Coming soon
Act s 49 Registration of a repository operator, a portal operator or a contracted service providerSystem Operator must register eligible applicants, may refuse for security risk, set conditions, specify repositories.
Act s 49(1) Operator must register an applicant that applied and is eligible for that kind.
Act s 49(1)(a) Registration requires an application under section 47 for that kind. Coming soon
Act s 49(1)(b) Registration requires eligibility for that kind under section 48. Coming soon
Act s 49(2) Operator may decline registration if it could endanger system security or integrity. Coming soon
Act s 49(3) The System Operator can attach conditions to a registration. Coming soon
Act s 49(4) A repository operator registration decision must list the repositories it covers. Coming soon
Act s 49(5) A registration decision is effective as soon as it is made. Coming soon
Act s 50 Condition about provision of information to System OperatorRegistered operators and providers must hand over a recipient's record information when the System Operator asks. Coming soon
Act s 50A Condition of registration—handling old records that are works subject to copyrightRepository operators must not make old copyright works available where use would infringe copyright.
Act s 50A(1) Rule covers works created before the Copyright Act provision commences. Coming soon
Act s 50A(2) Operator must not make an old work available if permitted uses would infringe its copyright.
Act s 50A(2)(a) Covers acts for purposes where the Act requires or authorises health information handling. Coming soon
Act s 50A(2)(b) Covers acts in a serious-threat situation permitted under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 50A(2)(c) Covers acts in a permitted health situation under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 50A(2)(d) Covers other healthcare or health information purposes prescribed by regulations. Coming soon
Act s 50A(3) Registered repository operators must comply with the copyright handling duty for old works as a registration condition. Coming soon
Act s 50B Condition of registration—handling old sound recordings and cinematograph films that are subject to copyrightRepository operators must not make pre-commencement recordings or films available where doing so would infringe copyright, subject to listed purposes.
Act s 50B(1) The restriction applies to sound recordings and films made before the Copyright Act provision commences. Coming soon
Act s 50B(2) Operators must not make old recordings or films available if copyright would be infringed, outside specified permitted purposes.
Act s 50B(2)(a) Copyright-infringing acts are excepted where done for purposes the Act requires or authorises for health information. Coming soon
Act s 50B(2)(b) Exception covering acts done in a permitted general situation involving serious threat to life, health or safety. Coming soon
Act s 50B(2)(c) Exception covering acts done in a permitted health situation under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
Act s 50B(2)(d) Exception for other healthcare or health information purposes prescribed by regulations. Coming soon
Act s 50B(3) Compliance with the old recordings and films restriction is a condition of repository operator registration. Coming soon
Act s 50C Liability where work uploaded in breach of section 50A or 50BPeople who suffer loss from breaches of the copyright provisions can sue the entity in court.
Act s 50C(1) Affected persons may bring a damages action against an entity contravening the copyright provisions, in listed courts.
Act s 50C(1)(a) The Federal Court of Australia is a permitted forum. Coming soon
Act s 50C(1)(b) The Federal Circuit and Family Court (Division 2) is a permitted forum. Coming soon
Act s 50C(1)(c) State or Territory courts with jurisdiction are permitted forums. Coming soon
Act s 50C(2) Claims must be started within six years of the loss or damage. Coming soon
Act s 50C(3) Damages may include costs of copyright infringement legal proceedings the person incurred. Coming soon
Act s 50D Authorisation to make health information available to the System OperatorRepository operators other than Medicare's chief executive may make held health information available to the System Operator. Coming soon
Act s 51 Cancellation or suspension of registrationSets out when the System Operator must or may cancel or suspend registrations.
Act s 51(1) Cancellation or suspension on requestSystem Operator must cancel or suspend registration when the registrant asks in writing. Coming soon
Act s 51(2) Cancellation or suspension if healthcare recipient no longer eligible, etc.Lists grounds on which the System Operator may cancel or suspend a healthcare recipient's registration.
Act s 51(2)(a) Ground: recipient no longer appears eligible to be registered. Coming soon
Act s 51(2)(b) Ground: recipient's identity no longer appears appropriately verified. Coming soon
Act s 51(2)(c) Ground: continued registration may compromise system security or integrity. Coming soon
Act s 51(2)(d) Ground: the recipient's consent has been withdrawn. Coming soon
Act s 51(2)(e) Ground: consent given by a representative who ceased acting and recipient did not reconsent.
Act s 51(2)(e)(i) The representative who gave consent has stopped being a representative. Coming soon
Act s 51(2)(e)(ii) The System Operator asked the recipient to give consent themselves. Coming soon
Act s 51(2)(e)(iii) The recipient did not give consent within a reasonable time. Coming soon
Act s 51(3) Cancellation or suspension if other entity no longer eligible, etc.Lists grounds for cancelling or suspending registration of entities other than recipients.
Act s 51(3)(a) Ground: entity no longer appears eligible for registration. Coming soon
Act s 51(3)(b) Ground: contravention, prevention of contravention, or protecting system security and integrity.
Act s 51(3)(b)(i) Entity has breached the Act or a registration condition. Coming soon
Act s 51(3)(b)(ii) Action is reasonably needed to prevent a contravention. Coming soon
Act s 51(3)(b)(iii) Action is otherwise appropriate to protect system security and integrity. Coming soon
Act s 51(3A) Cancellation or suspension if other entity no longer eligible, etc.System Operator may act against a provider organisation not shown able to meet its conditions. Coming soon
Act s 51(4) Suspension while investigating action in relation to healthcare recipient’s registrationRecipient's registration may be suspended while investigating possible action. Coming soon
Act s 51(5) Suspension while investigating action in relation to entity’s registrationOther entity's registration may be suspended during investigation of possible cancellation or suspension. Coming soon
Act s 51(6) Cancellation of registration of healthcare recipient on deathSystem Operator must cancel a recipient's registration once satisfied they have died. Coming soon
Act s 51(7) When cancellation or suspension takes effectCancellation or suspension takes effect when decided, or at a requested future time.
Act s 51(7)(a) Decision takes effect at the moment it is made. Coming soon
Act s 51(7)(b) For requested decisions, effect occurs at the future time the requester specified. Coming soon
Act s 52 Variation of registrationSystem Operator may vary registrations, including conditions, repositories or errors, taking effect as specified.
Act s 52(1) System Operator may vary registration on its own initiative or on request.
Act s 52(1)(a) Variation may impose conditions or additional conditions. Coming soon
Act s 52(1)(b) Variation may change or revoke existing conditions. Coming soon
Act s 52(1)(c) Variation may change which repositories a repository operator's registration covers. Coming soon
Act s 52(1)(d) Variation may fix an error or omission in the registration. Coming soon
Act s 52(2) Variation takes effect when made or at a requested later time.
Act s 52(2)(a) Variation takes effect when the decision is made. Coming soon
Act s 52(2)(b) Requested variations take effect at the specified future time. Coming soon
Act s 53 Notice of cancellation, suspension or variation of registration etc.System Operator must give notice and a chance to respond before cancelling, suspending or varying, except urgently.
Act s 53(1) Written notice before cancellation etc. other than in urgent circumstancesWritten notice is required before cancellation, suspension or variation, unless urgent.
Act s 53(1)(a) Notice is required before cancelling or suspending under listed section 51 provisions. Coming soon
Act s 53(1)(b) Notice is required before varying an entity's registration, except in urgent cases. Coming soon
Act s 53(2) Written notice before cancellation etc. other than in urgent circumstancesNotice must give reasons, may list corrective steps, and invite written submissions.
Act s 53(2)(a) Notice must say action is proposed and explain why. Coming soon
Act s 53(2)(b) Notice may specify steps the entity must take to address a contravention. Coming soon
Act s 53(2)(c) Notice must invite a written submission within a stated period. Coming soon
Act s 53(3) Written notice before cancellation etc. other than in urgent circumstancesNo decision may be made until the submission period has ended. Coming soon
Act s 53(4) Cancellation etc. in urgent circumstancesIn urgent circumstances the System Operator may act immediately by written notice.
Act s 53(4)(a) Urgent notice may cancel or suspend registration under listed provisions. Coming soon
Act s 53(4)(b) Urgent notice may vary an entity's registration. Coming soon
Act s 53(5) Cancellation etc. in urgent circumstancesUrgent decisions take effect when notice is given or at a later specified time.
Act s 53(5)(a) Urgent decision takes effect when notice is given. Coming soon
Act s 53(5)(b) Urgent decision takes effect at a later time if the notice specifies one. Coming soon
Act s 54 Effect of suspensionDescribes how suspension affects an entity's registered status for authorisation purposes and other provisions.
Act s 54(a) During suspension, entity is treated as unregistered for authorised collection, use and disclosure, with two exceptions.
Act s 54(a)(i) Exception: collection, use or disclosure on System Operator's request still applies. Coming soon
Act s 54(a)(ii) Exception: serious threat provision continues to apply. Coming soon
Act s 54(ab) Suspended provider organisations or repository operators are treated as unregistered for specified provisions. Coming soon
Act s 54(b) Suspended repository, portal or contracted service operators remain registered for the other provisions. Coming soon
Act s 55 My Health Records Rules may specify requirements after registration is cancelled or suspendedRules may set post-cancellation or suspension requirements, including record retention, transfer or disposal.
Act s 55(1) Rules may specify requirements applying after registration is cancelled or suspended. Coming soon
Act s 55(2) Rules cannot alter the effect of the suspension provision. Coming soon
Act s 55(3) Post-cancellation requirements may cover retention, transfer or disposal of records.
Act s 55(3)(a) Requirements may cover retention, transfer or disposal of My Health Records. Coming soon
Act s 55(3)(b) Requirements may cover retention, transfer or disposal of other records. Coming soon
Act s 56 The RegisterSystem Operator must establish and maintain a Register, possibly electronic and in parts.
Act s 56(1) System Operator must set up and maintain a Register. Coming soon
Act s 56(2) Register may be electronic and divided into separate parts. Coming soon
Act s 56(3) The Register is not a legislative instrument. Coming soon
Act s 57 Entries to be made in RegisterAfter registration decisions, System Operator must promptly enter required information in the Register.
Act s 57(a) Register entries must include administrative information needed for proper system operation. Coming soon
Act s 57(b) Register entries must include any information the Rules specify. Coming soon
Act s 58 Collection, use and disclosure of health information by the System OperatorSystem Operator may collect, use and disclose health information to populate registered recipients' records. Coming soon
Act s 58A Collection, use and disclosure of healthcare identifiers, identifying information and information identifying authorised representatives and nominated representativesTable authorises listed entities to handle healthcare identifiers and identifying information for system purposes.
Act s 58A(1) Listed entities may collect, use and disclose specified identifiers and information in stated circumstances.
Act s 58A(1) item 1 System Operator may handle identifying information and healthcare identifiers for My Health Record purposes. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 2 System Operator may handle information to decide whether someone is a representative. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 3 Repository and portal operators may disclose healthcare identifiers to system participants for system purposes. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 4 Healthcare identifiers service operator may exchange representative-status information with the System Operator. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 5 Medicare's chief executive may exchange identifying information with the System Operator for identity verification. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 6 Medicare's chief executive may exchange representative-relationship information with the System Operator. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 7 Medicare's chief executive may disclose recipient identifiers to participants to add health information. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 8 Veterans' Affairs and Defence may disclose identifying information to the System Operator for identity verification. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 9 Veterans' Affairs and Defence may collect and disclose identifiers to add prescribed information to records. Coming soon
Act s 58A(1) item 10 Prescribed entities may share identifying information with each other to help verify identity. Coming soon
Act s 58A(2) Listed government bodies must promptly tell the System Operator when identifying information they supplied later changes.
Act s 58A(2)(a) Applies to named bodies that disclosed information to the System Operator under the authorised-disclosure table.
Act s 58A(2)(a)(i) Covers the Chief Executive Medicare as a disclosing entity. Coming soon
Act s 58A(2)(a)(ii) Covers the Veterans' Affairs Department as a disclosing entity. Coming soon
Act s 58A(2)(a)(iii) Covers the Defence Department as a disclosing entity. Coming soon
Act s 58A(2)(a)(iv) Covers the healthcare identifiers service operator as a disclosing entity. Coming soon
Act s 58A(2)(a)(v) Covers any entity prescribed for item 10 of the disclosure table. Coming soon
Act s 58A(2)(b) Once the discloser learns the data changed, it must notify the System Operator quickly. Coming soon
Act s 59 Unauthorised collection, use and disclosure of health information included in a healthcare recipient’s My Health RecordProhibits knowingly or recklessly collecting, using or disclosing record health information without authorisation, with criminal and civil penalties.
Act s 59(1) No one may collect record health information from the system where unauthorised, knowingly or recklessly. Coming soon
Act s 59(2) No one may use or disclose health information obtained via the system without authorisation, knowingly or recklessly.
Act s 59(2)(a) Condition: the person got the information by using or accessing the record system. Coming soon
Act s 59(2)(b) Condition: the use or disclosure lacks authorisation and the person knows or is reckless about that. Coming soon
Act s 59(3) Fault ‐ based offenceBreaching the collection, use or disclosure ban is an offence carrying up to five years' imprisonment. Coming soon
Act s 59(4) Civil penaltyBreaching the collection, use or disclosure ban also attracts a civil penalty of 1,500 units. Coming soon
Act s 59A Unauthorised use of information included in a healthcare recipient’s My Health Record for prohibited purposeBans using record health information for prohibited purposes, whether obtained through the system or from copies stored elsewhere.
Act s 59A(1) Health information obtained through the system must not be used for a prohibited purpose. Coming soon
Act s 59A(1A) Prohibited-purpose ban also covers information first lawfully obtained via the system, then stored and retrieved elsewhere.
Act s 59A(1A)(a) Condition: a participant originally obtained the information through the system lawfully. Coming soon
Act s 59A(1A)(b) Condition: the information was afterwards stored so it could be retrieved without the system. Coming soon
Act s 59A(1A)(c) Condition: the person later got the information by those other routes; civil penalty applies. Coming soon
Act s 59A(2) The ban excludes the healthcare recipient themselves but still binds their nominated representative. Coming soon
Act s 60 Secondary disclosureProhibits using or disclosing record information that was unlawfully disclosed to you, if you know or are reckless.
Act s 60(1) Do not use or disclose information you know, or recklessly ignore, was disclosed to you unlawfully.
Act s 60(1)(a) Condition: the information reached the person through a disclosure breaching section 59(2). Coming soon
Act s 60(1)(b) Condition: the person knew or was reckless that the earlier disclosure was a breach. Coming soon
Act s 60(2) Exception: disclosure is allowed to help an appropriate authority investigate the original breach. Coming soon
Act s 60(3) Fault ‐ based offenceSecondary disclosure is an offence punishable by up to five years' imprisonment. Coming soon
Act s 60(4) Civil penaltySecondary disclosure also carries a civil penalty of 1,500 penalty units. Coming soon
Act s 61 Collection, use and disclosure for providing healthcareParticipants may handle record information to provide healthcare, following recipient or default access controls, excluding recipient-only notes.
Act s 61(1) Participants may collect, use and disclose record information for healthcare, consistent with applicable access controls.
Act s 61(1)(a) The handling must be for the purpose of providing healthcare to the recipient. Coming soon
Act s 61(1)(b) The handling must follow the recipient's access controls or, absent those, the default controls.
Act s 61(1)(b)(i) Access controls chosen by the registered recipient govern the handling. Coming soon
Act s 61(1)(b)(ii) Where none are set, default controls from the Rules or System Operator apply. Coming soon
Act s 61(2) This healthcare authority does not extend to notes only the recipient can see. Coming soon
Act s 62 Collection, use and disclosure to nominated representativeParticipants may disclose record information for any purpose to the recipient's nominated representative, subject to access controls.
Act s 62(a) The disclosure must go to the registered recipient's nominated representative. Coming soon
Act s 62(b) The disclosure must respect the recipient's access controls or the default controls.
Act s 62(b)(i) Access controls chosen by the registered recipient govern the disclosure. Coming soon
Act s 62(b)(ii) If no controls were set, defaults from the Rules or System Operator apply. Coming soon
Act s 63 Collection, use and disclosure for management of My Health Record systemParticipants may handle record information to manage or operate the system, or on System Operator request.
Act s 63(a) Handling for system management or operation is authorised if the recipient would reasonably expect it. Coming soon
Act s 63(b) Handling is authorised when responding to a System Operator request tied to its functions or powers. Coming soon
Act s 64 Collection, use and disclosure in the case of a serious threatParticipants may handle record information to address serious threats, with System Operator notice and timing limits, excluding recipient-only notes.
Act s 64(1) For serious threats to an individual, handling is allowed on reasonable belief, notifying the System Operator, within five days.
Act s 64(1)(a) Participant must reasonably believe handling is necessary for a serious individual threat and consent is impracticable.
Act s 64(1)(a)(i) Belief that handling is needed to lessen or prevent a serious threat to someone's life, health or safety. Coming soon
Act s 64(1)(a)(ii) Belief that obtaining the recipient's consent is unreasonable or impracticable. Coming soon
Act s 64(1)(b) Unless it is the System Operator, the participant must advise it of those beliefs. Coming soon
Act s 64(1)(c) The handling must occur within five days of giving that advice. Coming soon
Act s 64(2) Handling is authorised where reasonably believed necessary to lessen or prevent a serious public health or safety threat. Coming soon
Act s 64(3) Serious-threat authorities do not cover recipient-only notes. Coming soon
Act s 65 Collection, use and disclosure authorised by lawParticipants may handle record information when specified Commonwealth, State or Territory laws require or authorise it, excluding recipient-only notes.
Act s 65(1) Handling is authorised where a listed law requires or permits it, subject to section 69. Coming soon
Act s 65(2) Law-based authority does not extend to recipient-only notes. Coming soon
Act s 65(3) Lists the laws that count: this Act, Auditor-General, Ombudsman and Information Commissioner functions.
Act s 65(3)(a) This Act is a covered law. Coming soon
Act s 65(3)(b) The Auditor-General Act 1997 is a covered law. Coming soon
Act s 65(3)(c) The Ombudsman Act 1976 is a covered law. Coming soon
Act s 65(3)(d) Commonwealth laws supporting the Information Commissioner's functions over the system are covered. Coming soon
Act s 66 Collection, use and disclosure with healthcare recipient’s consentParticipants may disclose record information to the recipient, and handle it for any purpose with their consent.
Act s 66(1) Participants may disclose record information to the healthcare recipient for any purpose. Coming soon
Act s 66(2) With the recipient's consent, participants may collect, use and disclose their record information for any purpose. Coming soon
Act s 67 Collection, use and disclosure by a healthcare recipientA healthcare recipient may handle information in their own record for any purpose. Coming soon
Act s 68 Collection, use and disclosure for indemnity coverParticipants may handle record information for indemnity cover purposes, excluding recipient-only notes.
Act s 68(1) Handling record information is authorised for purposes relating to a provider's indemnity cover. Coming soon
Act s 68(2) Indemnity authority does not extend to recipient-only notes. Coming soon
Act s 69 Disclosure to courts and tribunalsSets when the System Operator must disclose to courts, tribunals and coroners, and protects participants from compelled disclosure.
Act s 69(1) System Operator must obey court or tribunal orders in specified proceedings types.
Act s 69(1)(a) Condition: a non-coroner court or tribunal directs the System Operator to disclose record information. Coming soon
Act s 69(1)(b) Condition: the order arises in proceedings of a listed kind.
Act s 69(1)(b)(i) Proceedings relating to this Act. Coming soon
Act s 69(1)(b)(ii) Proceedings about unauthorised access through the system. Coming soon
Act s 69(1)(b)(iia) Proceedings concerning a share by default provision. Coming soon
Act s 69(1)(b)(iii) Proceedings about providing indemnity cover to a healthcare provider. Coming soon
Act s 69(1)(c) Condition: the System Operator would otherwise be bound to comply, so it must comply. Coming soon
Act s 69(2) System Operator must comply with a coroner's order to disclose record information. Coming soon
Act s 69(3) Participants and recipients cannot be compelled to disclose record information to courts, outside the exceptions. Coming soon
Act s 69(4) Outside the exceptions, System Operator needs recipient consent before disclosing to a court or tribunal. Coming soon
Act s 69(5) Court and coroner orders cannot make the System Operator disclose recipient-only notes. Coming soon
Act s 69A Disclosure to designated entity under order by judicial officerSets how designated agencies may obtain record information through a judicial order served on the System Operator.
Act s 69A(1) System Operator must comply with a section 69A order presented by a designated agency or authority.
Act s 69A(1)(a) A designated entity is a Privacy Act agency or State or Territory authority. Coming soon
Act s 69A(1)(b) Courts, tribunals and coroners are excluded; the System Operator must obey the presented order. Coming soon
Act s 69A(2) Apart from these orders and covered laws, participants and recipients cannot be forced to disclose to designated entities. Coming soon
Act s 69A(3) The System Operator is not authorised to disclose recipient-only notes under this section. Coming soon
Act s 69A(4) System Operator must write a note whenever it uses or discloses personal information under this section. Coming soon
Act s 69A(5) Application for and making of orderA designated entity applies to a magistrate or eligible judge for a disclosure order.
Act s 69A(5)(a) A State or Territory magistrate may receive the application. Coming soon
Act s 69A(5)(b) A judge eligible under section 69B(2) may receive the application. Coming soon
Act s 69A(6) Application for and making of orderJudicial officer may grant the order only if sworn evidence and privacy balance conditions are met.
Act s 69A(6)(a) Entity must satisfy the officer on oath about its powers, necessity and lack of alternatives.
Act s 69A(6)(a)(i) Entity has information-demanding powers or warrant-executing duties as described in subsection (7). Coming soon
Act s 69A(6)(a)(ii) If relying on a demand power, the entity has already tried exercising it. Coming soon
Act s 69A(6)(a)(iii) The specific disclosure is reasonably necessary for something the entity is doing. Coming soon
Act s 69A(6)(a)(iv) No other effective way exists to get the information besides this order. Coming soon
Act s 69A(6)(b) Officer must find disclosure would not unreasonably intrude on the recipient's privacy, on balance. Coming soon
Act s 69A(7) Application for and making of orderDefines qualifying powers: legal power to require information, or routine authority to execute warrants.
Act s 69A(7)(a) Entity has a legal power, outside covered laws, to compel people to provide information. Coming soon
Act s 69A(7)(b) Entity's officers are ordinarily authorised to execute warrants to enter premises and seize items. Coming soon
Act s 69A(8) Application for and making of orderOfficer must not make the order until receiving any further information requested about the grounds. Coming soon
Act s 69A(9) Application for and making of orderThe order must name the recipient, the information, authorised officers, an expiry within six months, and purpose.
Act s 69A(9)(a) The order must identify the healthcare recipient. Coming soon
Act s 69A(9)(b) The order must specify exactly which information is to be disclosed. Coming soon
Act s 69A(9)(c) The order must empower entity officers to obtain the information from the System Operator. Coming soon
Act s 69A(9)(d) The order must set an expiry date no later than six months out. Coming soon
Act s 69A(9)(e) The order must state its purpose. Coming soon
Act s 69B Judicial officers for orders under section 69ASets how judges and magistrates may be nominated or arranged to perform section 69A functions.
Act s 69B(1) Eligible judge of a court created by the ParliamentA judge may give written consent to be nominated by the Attorney-General. Coming soon
Act s 69B(2) Eligible judge of a court created by the ParliamentAttorney-General may nominate consenting judges as eligible for section 69A orders. Coming soon
Act s 69B(3) Eligible judge of a court created by the ParliamentSuch a nomination is not a legislative instrument. Coming soon
Act s 69B(4) MagistratesMagistrates are not obliged to take on section 69A functions. Coming soon
Act s 69B(5) MagistratesGovernor-General may arrange with State and Territory leaders for magistrates to perform section 69A functions.
Act s 69B(5)(a) Arrangement with a State Governor for that State's magistrates to perform the functions. Coming soon
Act s 69B(5)(b) Arrangement with the ACT Chief Minister for ACT magistrates to perform the functions. Coming soon
Act s 69B(5)(c) Arrangement with the Northern Territory Administrator for Local Court judges to perform the functions. Coming soon
Act s 69B(6) Judicial officers exercising powers in personal capacityJudicial officers exercise these functions personally, not as a court.
Act s 69B(6)(a) Functions are conferred on the officer personally. Coming soon
Act s 69B(6)(b) Functions are not conferred on the officer as a court or its member. Coming soon
Act s 69B(7) Judicial officers exercising powers in personal capacityJudicial officers performing these functions receive the same protection and immunity as in court.
Act s 69B(7)(a) Immunity as if acting as the court the officer belongs to. Coming soon
Act s 69B(7)(b) Immunity as if acting as a member of that court. Coming soon
Act s 70 Disclosure in relation to unlawful activityLets the System Operator use or disclose record information about suspected unlawful activity, with limits and a written note.
Act s 70(3) System Operator may use or disclose health information when unlawful activity is suspected and use is reasonably necessary.
Act s 70(3)(a) Requires reason to suspect unlawful activity relating to the System Operator's functions. Coming soon
Act s 70(3)(b) Requires reasonable belief that disclosure is necessary for investigation or reporting concerns. Coming soon
Act s 70(3A) Disclosure is limited to what the recipient needs to identify the matter sufficiently.

Act s 111 Guidelines relating to the Information Commissioner’s enforcement powers etc.Information Commissioner must issue guidelines on enforcement powers and must consider them when exercising powers.
Act s 111(1) Commissioner must consider relevant guidelines when exercising powers under this Act or related ones. Coming soon
Act s 111(2) Commissioner must formulate enforcement guidelines as a legislative instrument. Coming soon
Act s 112 RegulationsGovernor-General may make regulations, after consulting the Ministerial Council, with capped penalties.
Act s 112(1) Governor-General may make regulations on matters required, permitted, or needed to give effect to the Act.
Act s 112(1)(a) Regulations may cover matters the Act requires or permits to be prescribed. Coming soon
Act s 112(1)(b) Regulations may cover matters necessary or convenient for carrying out the Act. Coming soon
Act s 112(2) Regulations may address any matter the Minister could cover in the Rules. Coming soon
Act s 112(3) Minister must consult the Ministerial Council before regulations are made. Coming soon
Act s 112(4) Regulations may set offence penalties up to 50 penalty units. Coming soon
Act s 112(5) Regulations may set civil penalties capped at 50 units for individuals, 250 for bodies corporate.
Act s 112(5)(a) Civil penalty cap for an individual is 50 penalty units. Coming soon
Act s 112(5)(b) Civil penalty cap for a body corporate is 250 penalty units. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 My Health Records for all healthcare recipientsSets out how the opt-out registration model is trialled, extended nationally, and how recipients are registered.
Act Sch 1 cl. 1 Trial of opt ‐ out modelMinister may apply the opt-out model to some recipient classes as a trial, after consultation.
Act Sch 1 cl. 1(1) Minister may make Rules applying the opt-out model to chosen classes of recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 1(2) Trial rules need Minister's satisfaction that the trial would yield evidence on participation value. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 1(3) Minister must consult the Health Chief Executives Forum before making trial rules. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 2 Minister may apply the opt ‐ out model to all healthcare recipients after trialAfter the trial, Minister may extend opt-out to all recipients, after consulting the Ministerial Council.
Act Sch 1 cl. 2(1) If the trial shows valuable participation, Minister may apply opt-out to all Australian recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 2(2) Minister may weigh trial evidence and other relevant matters in deciding.
Act Sch 1 cl. 2(2)(a) Minister may consider evidence gathered during the trial. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 2(2)(b) Minister may consider any other relevant matter. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 2(3) Minister must consult the Ministerial Council before making national opt-out rules. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 3 Registration of a healthcare recipient by the System OperatorSystem Operator may register a recipient only if eligible, identity verified, and no opt-out election; some bars apply.
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(1) Registration requires eligibility, appropriate identity verification, and opportunity to opt out with no election in force.
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(1)(a) Recipient must be eligible for registration under clause 4. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(1)(b) System Operator must be satisfied the recipient's identity was appropriately verified. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(1)(c) Recipient must have had a chance to opt out and have no election active.
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(1)(c)(i) Recipient must have been given the chance to elect not to be registered. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(1)(c)(ii) No election against registration may be in force. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(2) System Operator must not register a recipient if it risks system security or other prescribed circumstances.
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(2)(a) No registration where it may compromise system security or integrity, per the Rules. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 3(2)(b) Allows the Rules to prescribe further circumstances in which the System Operator registers a recipient. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 4 When a healthcare recipient is eligible for registrationSets eligibility for registration: an assigned healthcare identifier plus collected identifying details.
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(a) Eligibility requires a healthcare identifier assigned under the Healthcare Identifiers Act. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(b) Eligibility requires the System Operator to have collected specified personal details of the recipient.
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(b)(i) Full name must be collected. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(b)(ii) Date of birth must be collected. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(b)(iii) One of healthcare identifier, Medicare number or veterans' file number must be collected. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(b)(iv) Sex must be collected. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 4(b)(v) Any further information prescribed by regulations must be collected. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5 Healthcare recipient elects not to be registeredRecipients may opt out of registration by approved-form notice; the election's timing and end are set.
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(1) A recipient may notify the System Operator that they choose not to be registered. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(2) Opt-out notice must use the approved form, be lodged as specified, and meet any rule deadlines.
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(2)(a) Opt-out notice must be in the approved form. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(2)(b) Opt-out notice must be lodged where or how the form specifies. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(2)(c) Where Rules set a deadline or trigger for a class, the notice must meet it.
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(2)(c)(i) Condition: the Rules set a period or event for a class's opt-out. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(2)(c)(ii) Class members must give opt-out notice within the Rules' period or event. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(3) The opt-out takes effect on the day notice is given. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 5(4) The opt-out ends on the day the recipient applies to be registered. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6 Healthcare recipients may apply for registrationRecipients may apply for registration; the System Operator must register eligible verified applicants unless security or prescribed grounds bar it.
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(1) A recipient may apply to the System Operator to be registered. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(2) Application must use the approved form, include required documents and be lodged as specified.
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(2)(a) Application must be in the approved form. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(2)(b) Application must carry the information and documents the form requires. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(2)(c) Application must be lodged where or how the form specifies. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(3) System Operator must register a recipient whose application is valid, eligible and identity-verified.
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(3)(a) Condition: the recipient has made a compliant application. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(3)(b) Condition: the recipient meets the eligibility requirements of clause 4. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(3)(c) Condition: identity is satisfactorily verified, after which registration is mandatory. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(4) Registration is prohibited if it may endanger system security or in prescribed cases.
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(4)(a) No registration where it may compromise the system's security or integrity. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 6(4)(b) No registration in other circumstances the Rules prescribe. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 7 Collection, use and disclosure of health information by the System OperatorSystem Operator may handle health information to include it in a registered recipient's record. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8 Collection, use and disclosure of healthcare identifiers, identifying information and information identifying authorised representatives and nominated representativesTable authorises named entities to collect, use and disclose identifiers and identifying information for system purposes.
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) Table authorises named entities to collect, use and disclose identifiers and identifying information in stated circumstances.
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 1 System Operator may handle identifying information and identifiers of recipients, representatives and providers for system purposes. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 2 System Operator may handle information to decide whether someone is a representative. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 3 Repository and portal operators may handle healthcare identifiers and disclose them to participants for system purposes. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 4 Identifier service operator may exchange representative-status information with the System Operator. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 5 Medicare chief executive may exchange identifying information with the System Operator to help verify identity. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 6 Medicare chief executive may exchange representative-status information with the System Operator. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 7 Medicare chief executive may disclose identifiers to participants for uploads, unless a clause 13 election applies. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 8 Veterans' Affairs and Defence departments may disclose identifying information to help verify identity. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 9 Veterans' Affairs and Defence may disclose identifiers to participants for prescribed uploads, absent an election. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(1) item 10 Prescribed entities may share identifying information with each other to help verify identity. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2) Listed entities must promptly tell the System Operator when information they disclosed changes.
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(a) Applies when listed government or service entities have disclosed information to the System Operator.
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(a)(i) Chief Executive Medicare is a covered discloser. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(a)(ii) Veterans' Affairs Department is a covered discloser. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(a)(iii) Defence Department is a covered discloser. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(a)(iv) The Healthcare Identifiers Act service operator is a covered discloser. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(a)(v) Entities prescribed under item 10 are covered disclosers. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 8(2)(b) On learning disclosed information changed, the entity must inform the System Operator promptly. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 9 Authorisation for healthcare provider to upload health informationProvider organisations may upload records, including third-party details relevant to care, despite certain State consent laws.
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(1) Registered provider organisations may upload records, subject to recipient's no-upload advice and prescribed State laws.
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(1)(a) Upload authority is limited by the recipient's express advice not to upload records. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(1)(b) Upload authority is limited by State or Territory laws prescribed by regulations. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(2) Records may include directly relevant third-party health information, subject to prescribed State laws. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(3) Upload authorisation overrides State consent-form laws, except laws prescribed by regulations.
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(3)(a) Covers State laws requiring consent to be given expressly. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 9(3)(b) Covers State laws requiring consent in a particular manner, apart from prescribed ones. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 10 Registered repository operatorChief Executive Medicare's function is to seek registration as repository operator and operate it. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 11 Uploading health information to the repositoryMedicare chief executive may, at discretion, upload held health information to its repository. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 12 Making health information available to the System OperatorMedicare chief executive may make information available to the System Operator, but not if opted out.
Act Sch 1 cl. 12(1) Medicare chief executive may discretionarily make held health information available to the System Operator. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 12(2) Information must not be made available where the recipient's clause 13 election is in force. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13 Healthcare recipient may elect not to have health information disclosed to the System OperatorRecipients may opt out of Medicare-held information going to the System Operator, with notice rules.
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(1) A recipient may elect that Medicare-held health information not be made available. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(2) Election notice must use the approved form, be lodged as specified, and meet any rule deadlines.
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(2)(a) Election notice must be in the approved form. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(2)(b) Election notice must be lodged where or how the form specifies. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(2)(c) Where Rules set a deadline or trigger for a class, the notice must meet it.
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(2)(c)(i) Condition: the Rules set a period or event for a class's election. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(2)(c)(ii) Class members must give election notice within the Rules' period or event. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(3) The election starts on the day notice is given. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(4) The election ends on withdrawal notice or at a time the Rules prescribe.
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(4)(a) Election ends on the day the recipient gives withdrawal notice. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(4)(b) Election ends at any other time the Rules prescribe. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(5) Withdrawal notice must use the approved form and be lodged as specified.
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(5)(a) Withdrawal notice must be in the approved form. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 13(5)(b) Withdrawal notice must be lodged where or how the form specifies. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 14 Health information uploaded or made available may include details of healthcare providersUploaded or available information may name the providers who treated the recipient. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 15 Way in which repository operated not limited by this DivisionThis Division does not restrict how the repository is operated. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 16 Making health information available to the System OperatorOther registered repository operators may make held health information available to the System Operator. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17 References to other provisions of this ActLists how other Act provisions are adjusted for recipients covered by Part 2 of this Schedule.
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(a) Division 4 of Part 2 does not apply to such recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(b) Division 1 of Part 3 does not apply to such recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(c) Section 46 is read as referring to Part 2 of Schedule 1. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(d) Section 50D does not apply to such recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(e) Upload-consent paragraphs 51(2)(d) and (e) do not apply to such recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(f) Section 57 treats Schedule registration decisions like Part 3 registration decisions. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(g) Division 6 of Part 3 does not apply to such recipients. Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(h) Refusals under Part 2 of the Schedule count as refusals under section 41 for paragraph 97(1)(b). Coming soon
Act Sch 1 cl. 17(i) Recipients registered under the Schedule count as registered healthcare recipients under the Act. Coming soon
Rules My Health Records Rules 2026
Rules s 1 NameGives the instrument's name as the My Health Records Rules 2026. Coming soon
Rules s 2 CommencementExplains commencement of provisions according to a table; column 3 notes are not part of instrument.
Rules s 2(1) Each provision commences as stated in the table's second column. Coming soon
Rules s 2(2) Third-column information in the table is not part of the instrument. Coming soon
Rules s 3 AuthorityStates the instrument is made under the My Health Records Act 2012. Coming soon
Rules s 4 SchedulesInstruments listed in Schedules are amended or repealed as the Schedule items say. Coming soon
Rules s 5 DefinitionsDefines terms used in the Rules, such as access list, material change and interoperability requirements. Coming soon
Rules s 6 Definition of authorised representative of a healthcare recipient—persons to which healthcare identifier not required to have been assignedProfessional representatives need no healthcare identifier to qualify as authorised representatives. Coming soon
Rules s 7 Definition of nominated representative of a healthcare recipient—persons to which healthcare identifier not required to have been assignedProfessional representatives need no healthcare identifier to qualify as nominated representatives. Coming soon
Rules s 8 Access controls set by registered healthcare recipients for access by healthcare provider organisations and nominated representativesSets requirements for recipient-controlled access restrictions, hidden restricted records and access notifications.
Rules s 8(1) PurposeStates that this section sets requirements for recipient access control mechanisms. Coming soon
Rules s 8(2) Application of default access controlsDefault access controls apply wherever the recipient has not set their own controls. Coming soon
Rules s 8(3) Controls for access to a recipient’s My Health RecordRecipients must be able to restrict access to their record and lift restrictions per occasion.
Rules s 8(3)(a) Recipients must be able to restrict access to their whole record. Coming soon
Rules s 8(3)(b) Recipients must be able to lift a restriction for a particular occasion. Coming soon
Rules s 8(4) Controls for access to certain information or records in a recipient’s My Health RecordRecipients must be able to restrict specific information or records and lift that restriction occasionally.
Rules s 8(4)(a) Recipients must be able to restrict access to particular information or a record. Coming soon
Rules s 8(4)(b) Recipients must be able to lift a restriction on particular information for one occasion. Coming soon
Rules s 8(5) Controls for access to certain information or records in a recipient’s My Health RecordRestricted records must stay undetectable to providers by viewing, except in listed exceptions.
Rules s 8(5)(a) Exception: organisation is on the access list and recipient permitted it to access the item.
Rules s 8(5)(a)(i) Condition: the organisation appears on the recipient's access list. Coming soon
Rules s 8(5)(a)(ii) Condition: the recipient has specified that the organisation may access the item. Coming soon
Rules s 8(5)(b) Exception: recipient lifted the restriction for the organisation on that occasion. Coming soon
Rules s 8(5)(c) Exception: the organisation itself uploaded the information or record. Coming soon
Rules s 8(6) Controls for access to certain information or records in a recipient’s My Health RecordAn uploading organisation keeps access to its restricted upload without the recipient lifting the restriction. Coming soon
Rules s 8(7) Electronic notification of accessing or viewing of informationRecipients must be able to receive electronic notices of certain provider or representative access.
Rules s 8(7)(a) Notification when a provider organisation first accesses the record or accesses it under section 64.
Rules s 8(7)(a)(i) Notify when an organisation not on the access list first accesses the record. Coming soon
Rules s 8(7)(a)(ii) Notify when an organisation accesses the record for purposes of section 64 of the Act. Coming soon
Rules s 8(7)(b) Notify the recipient when a nominated representative views health information in the record. Coming soon
Rules s 9 Default access controlsDefines default access controls: access list, three-year removal, uploader access, and recipient deletion.
Rules s 9(1) PurposeStates that this section sets requirements for default access control mechanisms. Coming soon
Rules s 9(2) Default access controls for access by healthcare provider organisations, authorised representatives and nominated representativesDefault controls must allow treating providers access, maintain a viewable access list, and expire inactive entries.
Rules s 9(2)(a) Default controls must permit providers treating the recipient to access the record. Coming soon
Rules s 9(2)(b) Default controls must include an access list of organisations providing the recipient care. Coming soon
Rules s 9(2)(c) Recipients must be able to view their record's access list. Coming soon
Rules s 9(2)(d) Organisations not accessing the record for three years must be removed from the access list. Coming soon
Rules s 9(2)(e) Delisted organisations may request System Operator access to records they uploaded. Coming soon
Rules s 9(3) Default access controls permitting healthcare recipients to delete health informationDefault controls must let recipients delete health information or records from their record. Coming soon
Rules s 10 Circumstances for automatic suspension of access to a healthcare recipient’s My Health RecordAccess controls must specify circumstances triggering automatic suspension of representative access.
Rules s 10(1) PurposeStates that this section sets requirements for suspension-related access control mechanisms. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) CircumstancesAccess controls must automatically suspend access for listed entities in tabulated circumstances.
Rules s 10(2) item 1 Suspend an authorised representative and related nominees when their identifier is marked deceased. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 2 Suspend a nominated representative whose healthcare identifier is marked deceased. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 3 Suspend a person while the System Operator investigates their nominated representative status. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 4 Suspend an authorised representative and nominees during an investigation into cancelling their access. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 5 Suspend a nominated representative while investigating whether to cancel their access. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 6 Suspend a person and their nominees when information questions their authorised representative status. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 7 Suspend an authorised representative and nominees on notified serious risk to safety. Coming soon
Rules s 10(2) item 8 Suspend a nominated representative on notified serious risk to life, health or safety. Coming soon
Rules s 11 Circumstances for automatic cancellation of access to a healthcare recipient’s My Health RecordAccess controls must specify circumstances triggering automatic cancellation of representative access.
Rules s 11(1) PurposeStates that this section sets requirements for cancellation-related access control mechanisms. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) CircumstancesAccess controls must automatically cancel access for listed entities in tabulated circumstances.
Rules s 11(2) item 1 Cancel an authorised representative and related nominees when their identifier is retired. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 2 Cancel a nominated representative whose healthcare identifier is retired. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 3 Cancel a nominated representative's access upon notification of their death. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 4 Cancel a minor's representative and nominees if not expected to qualify when recipient turns 18. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 5 Cancel former representatives and nominees when recipient turns 18 without qualifying satisfaction. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 6 Cancel representative and nominees when recipient turns 18 or withdraws the nomination. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 7 Cancel a person and nominees when the System Operator is no longer satisfied of their status. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 8 Cancel an authorised representative and nominees who say they no longer wish to act. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 9 Cancel a nominated representative who notifies they no longer wish to act. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 10 Cancel a former authorised representative and nominees for reasons not covered elsewhere. Coming soon
Rules s 11(2) item 11 Cancel a person who is no longer a nominated representative for any other reason. Coming soon
Rules s 12 Purpose of this DivisionThis Division gives the System Operator additional functions. Coming soon
Rules s 13 Deleting information or a record in the My Health Record system in certain circumstancesSystem Operator may delete records that are defamatory, threaten security, or were uploaded unlawfully.
Rules s 13(a) Deletion permitted where the information contains a defamatory statement. Coming soon
Rules s 13(b) Deletion permitted where the information affects system security or integrity. Coming soon
Rules s 13(c) Deletion permitted for unlawfully uploaded records whose removal reduces clinical risk.
Rules s 13(c)(i) Condition: record was uploaded in breach of paragraph 45(ba) of the Act. Coming soon
Rules s 13(c)(ii) Condition: deletion is needed to reduce clinical risk to the recipient. Coming soon
Rules s 14 Suspending access to the My Health Record system if security, integrity or operations are or may be compromisedSystem Operator may suspend system access when security or integrity is compromised, with notice and restoration.
Rules s 14(1) Suspension for certain entitiesSystem Operator may suspend access for recipients, representatives or participants if security is compromised.
Rules s 14(1)(a) Suspension may apply to a healthcare recipient. Coming soon
Rules s 14(1)(b) Suspension may apply to an authorised representative. Coming soon
Rules s 14(1)(c) Suspension may apply to a nominated representative. Coming soon
Rules s 14(1)(d) Suspension may apply to a system participant. Coming soon
Rules s 14(2) Suspension for certain entitiesGives examples of compromise: participant IT or credential problems, identity issues, interoperability non-compliance.
Rules s 14(2)(a) Compromise includes a security problem with a participant's IT systems or credentials. Coming soon
Rules s 14(2)(b) Compromise includes problems verifying a recipient's or representative's identity. Coming soon
Rules s 14(2)(c) Compromise includes a participant failing interoperability requirements. Coming soon
Rules s 14(3) Suspension for certain entitiesParticipants failing interoperability requirements may be suspended fully or partly. Coming soon
Rules s 14(4) Notice requirementsSystem Operator must notify suspended entities, subject to exceptions. Coming soon
Rules s 14(5) Notice requirementsSuspension notice must be written, prompt, and state reasons and restoration steps.
Rules s 14(5)(a) Suspension notice must be in writing. Coming soon
Rules s 14(5)(b) Suspension notice must be given as soon as practicable. Coming soon
Rules s 14(5)(c) Notice must state suspension reasons and steps required before restoration.
Rules s 14(5)(c)(i) Notice must state the reasons for suspension. Coming soon
Rules s 14(5)(c)(ii) Notice must state steps required before access is restored. Coming soon
Rules s 14(6) Notice requirementsNotice exception: minor operational matter unlikely to last over 24 hours. Coming soon
Rules s 14(7) Notice requirementsNotice exception: many recipients affected and the public has been notified.
Rules s 14(7)(a) Condition: suspension affects a significant number of healthcare recipients. Coming soon
Rules s 14(7)(b) Condition: the System Operator notifies the general public. Coming soon
Rules s 14(8) Restoring access following suspensionAccess must be restored promptly once the compromise or risk has ended. Coming soon
Rules s 15 Providing a mechanism to access My Health Record systemSystem Operator may offer a mechanism for registered providers to access the system. Coming soon
Rules s 16 Matters System Operator to have regard toLists identity-related matters the System Operator considers, concerning identifiers and identity evidence.
Rules s 16(a) For a child, consider the birth mother's identifier and identity evidence.
Rules s 16(a)(i) Consider whether the child's birth mother has a healthcare identifier. Coming soon
Rules s 16(a)(ii) Consider whether identity evidence confirms the birth mother. Coming soon
Rules s 16(b) For other recipients, consider their identifier and identity evidence.
Rules s 16(b)(i) Consider whether the recipient has a healthcare identifier. Coming soon
Rules s 16(b)(ii) Consider whether identity evidence confirms the recipient. Coming soon
Rules s 17 Purpose of this SubdivisionSets registration eligibility requirements for healthcare provider organisations. Coming soon
Rules s 18 Organisation officers must have authority to act on behalf of organisationOrganisation officers must be authorised to act for the organisation with the System Operator.
Rules s 18(1) Organisations that are seed organisations for a network or are not part of a networkApplies the authority requirement to seed organisations and non-network organisations. Coming soon
Rules s 18(2) Organisations that are seed organisations for a network or are not part of a networkResponsible officer and maintenance officer must be authorised to deal with the System Operator for standalone or seed organisations.
Rules s 18(2)(a) The organisation's responsible officer must be authorised to act in dealings with the System Operator. Coming soon
Rules s 18(2)(b) The organisation's maintenance officer must be authorised to act in dealings with the System Operator. Coming soon
Rules s 18(3) Organisations that are network organisations within a networkSubsection (4) applies to organisations that are network members within a network. Coming soon
Rules s 18(4) Organisations that are network organisations within a networkNetwork organisation's responsible officer, its own maintenance officer and the seed's maintenance officer must be authorised.
Rules s 18(4)(a) Network organisation's responsible officer must be authorised to deal with the System Operator. Coming soon
Rules s 18(4)(b) Network organisation's own maintenance officer must be authorised to deal with the System Operator. Coming soon
Rules s 18(4)(c) The seed organisation's maintenance officer must also be authorised for the network organisation's dealings. Coming soon
Rules s 19 Organisation must give System Operator and service operator certain informationOrganisation must supply the System Operator a list of authorised providers, and seeds supply network linkages, in approved form.

Rules s 19(1)(a) Give the System Operator a list of individual providers authorised to access the system through the organisation. Coming soon
Rules s 19(1)(b) Seed organisations must give the service operator a record of linkages among network organisations. Coming soon
Rules s 19(2) The provider list and linkage record must use the approved form. Coming soon

Rules s 21 Organisation must have security and access policyOrganisation needs a written, auditable security and access policy covering user authorisation, training, safeguards and risk handling.

Rules s 21(1)(b) The policy must be drafted so performance against it can be audited. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2) Lists the matters the policy must cover: authorisation, training, legal compliance, security measures and risk strategies.

Rules s 21(2)(a)(i) Account suspension or deactivation procedure for when a user leaves the organisation. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(a)(ii) Account suspension or deactivation procedure when a user's security is compromised. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(a)(iii) Account suspension or deactivation procedure when duties no longer need system access. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(a)(iv) Account suspension or deactivation procedure when an individual provider stops being linked to the organisation. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(b) Policy must set out user training before access, annually, and after significant changes.
Rules s 21(2)(b)(i) Users must be trained before being authorised to access the system. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(b)(ii) Users must receive training every year. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(b)(iii) Users must be retrained after significant changes to the law or the system. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(c) Policy must describe processes preventing contravention of sections 74 and 75 of the Act. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(d) Policy must describe physical, information and cyber security measures, including account management, maintenance, encryption, backup and review.
Rules s 21(2)(d)(i) Policy must cover user account management practices listed in subsection (4). Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(d)(ii) Policy must cover regular system maintenance. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(d)(iii) Policy must cover data protection, including encryption and regular backups. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(d)(iv) Policy must cover monitoring and reviewing the security measures. Coming soon
Rules s 21(2)(e) Policy must set strategies to quickly identify, act on and report security risks to management. Coming soon
Rules s 21(3) Training to be provided to usersRequired user training covers responsible use, legal obligations and consequences of breaches.
Rules s 21(3)(a) Training must cover accurate and responsible use of the system. Coming soon
Rules s 21(3)(b) Training must cover legal obligations of organisations and users. Coming soon
Rules s 21(3)(c) Training must cover consequences of breaching those obligations. Coming soon
Rules s 21(4) User account management practices to be implementedSets required user account management practices: least access, unique identity, strong passwords, deactivation, suspension, review, training.

Rules s 21(4)(b) Give each user a unique identity protected by a password or equivalent. Coming soon

Rules s 21(4)(d) Deactivate accounts of users no longer authorised to access the system. Coming soon
Rules s 21(4)(e) Suspend user access promptly once an account or password is known compromised. Coming soon
Rules s 21(4)(f) Review the account management practices at least once a year. Coming soon
Rules s 21(4)(g) Make sure users know and are trained in the account practices. Coming soon

Reuse: Official Australian Government text, free to read; reuse terms in the publisher's terms of use (not re-checked); cite IDs and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Slop to pop: design patterns: anti-patterns sloptopop converts into design patterns today, with the run that proves each one.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.

This site runs no JavaScript except htmx on the pricing page, to send the waitlist form; every animation is CSS. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
